title: Exceptional base change for towers and integral coefficients
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum: $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic $p$, and $\ell\ne p$ is prime [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y,Y'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and let $v:Y'\to Y$ be any $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Set $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $u:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, so $fu=vf'$; use a compactification $f=pj$ and its pullback for $f'$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. No smoothness, flatness or properness of $v$ is assumed.

Use the ordinary derived categories of varying-coefficient strict towers and their uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories $\Dctf(-_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$; normalization means that every derived reduction map is invertible [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Tower pullback is exact levelwise finite constant-ring pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]; $Rf_{!,\bullet}$ and $f^!_\bullet$ mean [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels, det-sp-tower-gluing]. Finite exceptional base change means the counit transpose of inverse compact-support exchange [lem-pur-smb-extraordinary, det-sp-mixed-base-change]. At integral coefficients use the completed coefficient sheaf, derived-complete constructible category and completed pullback [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The integral exceptional functor is the right adjoint of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], identified counit-preservingly with $H_f$ of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. Then: 

1. extension by zero and proper base change give a natural isomorphism
   $\beta_{f,\bullet}:v_\bullet^*Rf_{!,\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}R(f')_{!,\bullet}u_\bullet^*$ of
   functors $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)\to\Dctf(Y'_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$;
2. the transpose of $v_\bullet^*(\varepsilon_{f,\bullet})\circ\beta_{f,\bullet}^{-1}$ under
   the tower adjunction for $f'$ is a natural isomorphism
   $e_{f,\bullet}:u_\bullet^*f_\bullet^!\xrightarrow{\sim}(f')_\bullet^!v_\bullet^*$, whose level $n$
   is the finite exceptional base change $e_{f,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}$, and which is
   compatible with the reduction maps (hence preserves normalized towers);
3. for $E=\Ql$ and $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Zl)$, $R\varprojlim$ of $e_{f,\bullet}(\operatorname{red}_YK)$ is
   an isomorphism $u_{\Zl}^*f^!_{\Zl}K\xrightarrow{\sim}(f')^!_{\Zl}v^*_{\Zl}K$ in
   $\Dbc(X',\Zl)$, the integral exceptional base change, that is, the transpose under
   $R(f')_{!,\Zl}\dashv(f')^!_{\Zl}$ of $v_{\Zl}^*(\varepsilon_{f,\Zl}(K))\circ\beta_{f,\Zl}(f^!_{\Zl}K)^{-1}$.
   Here the integral compact-support base change
   $\beta_{f,\Zl}(M):v_{\Zl}^*Rf_{!,\Zl}M\xrightarrow{\sim}R(f')_{!,\Zl}u_{\Zl}^*M$ ($M\in\Dbc(X,\Zl)$)
   is the coefficient transport of $\beta_{f,\bullet}(\operatorname{red}_XM)$: the unique map whose
   reduction, under the reduction identifications for $Rf_{!,\Zl}$ of
   [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower] and the reconstruction counit for completed pullback, is
   $\beta_{f,\bullet}(\operatorname{red}_XM)$; it exists and is unique by the equivalence
   [det-sp-normalized-equivalence].

proof.text: Put $F_f=Rf_{!,\bullet}$ and $G_f=f^!_\bullet$. The pullback compactification $c'$ exists by [def-cbc-compact-support-square]; [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1) makes $f'$ smooth of the same relative dimension $d$. All four schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to their structure maps over the field $k$ (a field has only the ideals $0,(1)$). Their finite levels have etale-origin witnesses by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], since $A_n$ is finite. Uniform cohomological bounds make each tower bounded below in the ordinary tower derived category, whose cohomology is levelwise [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Pullback along $u,v$ preserves the finite constructible Tor interval by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], and the cohomological interval by exactness [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Consequently it preserves the stated tower category. The tensor-pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the coefficient quotient, identifies pullback of $C_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\to C_m$ with the reduction map of the pulled-back tower. These identifications are natural in the quotient, so pullback also preserves normalized towers.

Use the specified actual tower exchange of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2b), constructed from the proper counit mate and open extension for $c,c'$. Step 1 supplies its bounded-below input and an etale-origin witness at every finite level; compatible choices of these witnesses are unnecessary. This gives the isomorphism $\beta_{f,\bullet}:v^*_\bullet F_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}u^*_\bullet$, whose evaluations are the finite compact-support exchanges. The same statement's clause (1) identifies $F_f$ and $F_{f'}$ with the compactification operations used in [det-sp-tower-gluing]. That adjunction makes these functors defined on the tower ctf categories. Thus the ambient exchange restricts to the functors in clause (1) of the item.

source.place: (1): compactification exchange and its finite evaluations

proof.text: For a tower $K$ on $Y$, define $q_K=v^*_\bullet(\varepsilon_{f,K})\,\beta_{f,\bullet}(G_fK)^{-1}:F_{f'}u^*_\bullet G_fK\to v^*_\bullet K$. Its unique transpose under $F_{f'}\dashv G_{f'}$ of [det-sp-tower-gluing] is $e_K$, and explicitly $e_K=G_{f'}(q_K)\eta_{f',u^*G_fK}$. Naturality of $\beta$, the counit, and the unit makes this family natural. The evaluation comparisons in [det-sp-tower-gluing](3) and [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](1),(2) carry this formula to $G_{f',n}(v_n^*\varepsilon_{f,n}\,\beta_{f,n}^{-1})\eta_{f',n}$; this is the finite counit transpose, with the adjunction normalization in the item. Its invertibility is [lem-pur-smb-extraordinary], applied at $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{en}$, where $\ell$ is a unit times $\varpi_E^e$. It applies to $K_n$ in the finite ctf category, the same global field and smooth morphism, and arbitrary $v$. Hence each evaluation of the already constructed tower map $e_K$ is invertible. Clause (3) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] implies $e_K$ is invertible. This uses evaluation conservativity only after constructing $e_K$ by an actual tower adjunction.

Write $T_{nm}=-\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$, $r=r^K_{n,m}:T_{nm}K_n\to K_m$ and $P=u^*G_fK$, $Q=G_{f'}v^*K$. By [det-sp-tower-gluing](3), their reductions are $r^P_{n,m}=u_m^*G_{f,m}(r)\,u_m^*c^f_{n,m}(K_n)$ and $r^Q_{n,m}=G_{f',m}(v_m^*r)\,c^{f'}_{n,m}(v_n^*K_n)$, after the pullback/tensor identifications of Step 1. Apply the second identity of [det-sp-mixed-base-change] to the actual, possibly nonflat quotient $A_n\to A_m$. Composing that identity with $G_{f',m}(v_m^*r)$ and using naturality of $e_{f,m}$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
r^Q_{n,m}\,T_{nm}(e_{f,n}(K_n))
&=G_{f',m}(v_m^*r)\,e_{f,m}(T_{nm}K_n)\,u_m^*c^f_{n,m}(K_n)\\
&=e_{f,m}(K_m)\,u_m^*G_{f,m}(r)\,u_m^*c^f_{n,m}(K_n)
=e_{f,m}(K_m)\,r^P_{n,m}.
\end{aligned}$$
This is the claimed reduction square; no equality of derived tower maps is inferred from equality of their evaluations. For normalized input $K$, [det-sp-tower-gamma](3) makes $G_fK$ normalized, and Step 1 makes $P$ normalized. The square just proved and the invertibility of both horizontal maps make each reduction of $Q$ invertible. The ctf bounds of $Q$ already follow from Step 1 and the tower adjunction.

source.place: (2): explicit mixed reduction square and normalized subcategory

proof.text: Now put $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, write $r_T=\operatorname{red}_T$ and $L_T=R\varprojlim$, and use the equivalence [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. Its Noetherian hypothesis holds by Step 1. For $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathbf Z_\ell)$, [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection] gives the normalized tower $G_fr_YK$, the integral object $H_fK=L_XG_fr_YK$, the comparison $r_XH_fK\simeq G_fr_YK$, and $Rf_{!,\mathbf Z_\ell}\dashv H_f$ with its unit and counit transported from the tower adjunction. The right adjoint $f^!_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] is for the same compact-support functor: [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower](2) identifies that functor with $L_YF_fr_X$. Thus [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] gives the unique counit-preserving identification $f^!_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\simeq H_f$, and likewise for $f'$. Use these identifications throughout the remaining calculation; they transport the adjunctions, not merely their objects.

source.place: (3): integral adjunction and its counit-preserving normalization

proof.text:
For a morphism $h:U\to V$, put $C_K=h_\bullet^*r_VK$. Step 1 shows that $C_K$ is a normalized constructible tower for $K\in\Dbc(V,\mathbf Z_\ell)$, using [det-sp-normalized-equivalence] for $r_VK$. By the definition [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], completed pullback is $h^*_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K=L_UC_K$: apply termwise finite pullback to the single reduction complex and then take total derived inverse limit, with its quotient transitions. The reconstruction equivalence therefore shows directly that this pullback is constructible and gives an isomorphism of actual derived towers
$$r_Uh^*_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K=r_UL_UC_K\xrightarrow{\epsilon^{r,L}_{C_K}}C_K=h_\bullet^*r_VK.$$
This is the counit of [det-sp-normalized-equivalence], natural in the entire tower, rather than a lift inferred from individual reductions. Together with Step 5, for $h=u,v$ this supplies
$$a_K:r_{X'}(u_{\mathbf Z_\ell}^*f^!_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}u_\bullet^*G_fr_YK=P_K,\qquad b_K:r_{X'}((f')^!_{\mathbf Z_\ell}v_{\mathbf Z_\ell}^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f'}v_\bullet^*r_YK=Q_K.$$
Apply $L_{X'}$ to $e_{r_YK}:P_K\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_K$ and conjugate by these isomorphisms and the reconstruction units. This constructs a natural integral isomorphism $E_K$ with $r_{X'}E_K=b_K^{-1}e_{r_YK}a_K$. A functor takes an inverse pair to an inverse pair, so $E_K$ is invertible. This is precisely $R\varprojlim e_{f,\bullet}(r_YK)$ under the specified reconstruction identifications.

source.place: (3): pullback reductions and reconstruction of the isomorphism

proof.text:
Identify its transpose without commuting a Hom set with an infinite limit. For $M\in\Dbc(X,\mathbf Z_\ell)$, [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower](2) and Step 6 identify the reductions of $v_{\mathbf Z_\ell}^*Rf_{!,\mathbf Z_\ell}M$ and $R(f')_{!,\mathbf Z_\ell}u_{\mathbf Z_\ell}^*M$ with $v_\bullet^*F_fr_XM$ and $F_{f'}u_\bullet^*r_XM$. Both towers are normalized by [det-sp-tower-gamma](3) and Step 1. By the item's statement, $\beta_{f,\mathbf Z_\ell}(M)$ is the reconstruction of $\beta_{f,\bullet}(r_XM)$ through the equivalence [det-sp-normalized-equivalence], under these identifications: full faithfulness of $r_{Y'}$ on $\Dbc(Y',\mathbf Z_\ell)$ gives a unique integral arrow with that reduction, and it is invertible because $\beta_{f,\bullet}$ is (Step 2). This is the coefficient transport by which the source's proof, paragraph (3), reads the integral compact-support exchange. The Hom bijections of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection] send an integral arrow to its reduced arrow with these operation comparisons inserted, and send the integral counit to the tower counit. Consequently reduction of the integral transpose $\varepsilon_{f',v^*K}\,R(f')_!(E_K)$ is exactly
$$\varepsilon_{f',\bullet}\,F_{f'}(e_{r_YK})=v_\bullet^*(\varepsilon_{f,\bullet})\,\beta_{f,\bullet}(G_fr_YK)^{-1},$$
by the defining transpose equation of Step 3. The right side is the reduction of $v_{\mathbf Z_\ell}^*(\varepsilon_{f,\mathbf Z_\ell})\,\beta_{f,\mathbf Z_\ell}(f^!_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K)^{-1}$ by Step 5 and the just specified reconstruction of $\beta$. Faithfulness of $r_{Y'}$ in [det-sp-normalized-equivalence] proves equality of these integral arrows. Thus $E_K$ is exactly the exceptional base-change counit transpose, proving clause (3) with its stated normalization.

source.place: (3): explicit reduction of the transpose, using full faithfulness rather than levelwise faithfulness

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs (1)–(3), expanded with precise coefficient domains and an explicit reduction-square and integral-transpose calculation

split_report.summary: Retained all three conclusions and made the standing Cartesian-square, finite-field, smoothness and coefficient domains explicit. Reused only existing nodes. Constructed the actual tower mate before evaluating; cited finite canonical exceptional invertibility separately from the mixed identity; wrote the reduction square including the input transition. Reconstructed the integral arrow and computed its transpose through the fully faithful reduction equivalence. No faithfulness of finite-level evaluation or automatic preservation of invertibility by taking mates is assumed. Integral f! is identified with H counit-preservingly, rather than silently identifying coefficient models. The integral pullback comparison is constructed using the reconstruction counit on an actual normalized tower, avoiding a lift from finite-level maps.
split_report.blueprint: The seven steps expand the three paragraphs (1) compactification tower exchange, (2) counit transpose and mixed reduction compatibility, and (3) normalized-tower reconstruction of integral exceptional base change. This realizes the tower-base-change portion of unit sk-prop-sp-purity-bc step 1; it does not change the unit route or claim the unit statement.

statement_correction.what: The imported statement has unbound f,u,v,f′,X,Y,Y′,ell and no domain beyond “as in the sketch”, so it is not a self-contained proposition. For example, without smoothness the claimed exceptional base-change conclusion need not hold, and without finite type the chosen compact-support interfaces are unavailable. The corrected preamble copies the unit and purity standing context, retains arbitrary v in that context and every original conclusion, and distinguishes ordinary finite tower coefficients from completed integral coefficients.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q107-2ef059d96 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against the source tower lemma, paragraphs (1)-(3), the unit sk-prop-sp-purity-bc, and every cited node statement. The repaired statement is self-contained and not weakened: the smooth square comes from the unit, k is the closure of a finite field as in def-pur-conventions and both citers, v is arbitrary, and the coefficient categories are kept apart. The counterexample showing smoothness is needed (closed immersion of the origin into A^1) checks out. Steps 1-6 are correct. Step 2: shriek-levels (2b) has the right hypotheses. Step 3: the transpose is built before it is evaluated; lem-pur-smb-extraordinary, whose step 6 shows its canonical comparison is the counit transpose, makes each level invertible, and conservativity is used only on that constructed map. Step 4: I recomputed the reduction square from the mixed identity (2) and naturality. Steps 5-6: the two right adjoints are for the same integral Rf_! (direct-image-tower (2) and the def-weil-integral definition agree), so the unique counit-preserving comparison applies; completed pullback is the limit of the pulled-back tower, and the counit of the normalized equivalence gives the comparison. FIX (E5/C4-type): clause (3) named 'the integral exceptional base change' without fixing the integral compact-support exchange beta_Zl, and step 7 defined it inside the proof by tower reconstruction. The DAG has a separate def-cbc-completed-exchange-map and no node equating the two. Following source paragraph (3) and def-pur-conventions (integral versions are coefficient transports), I wrote this into clause (3): beta_Zl is the unique integral map whose reduction is beta_bullet(red_X M), via det-sp-normalized-equivalence and det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower, both added to stmt_deps (already proof deps, so no cycle). Step 7 now uses that and says why the map exists and is unique. Comparison with def-cbc-completed-exchange-map is not claimed and no citer needs it. Also noted: the report misses the citer thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace; its use of the tower clauses is compatible. Accepted tool uses: lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude and prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint. No new nodes, no SGA.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
